items.rationale: The SDK reads the key from the ANTHROPIC_API_KEY environment variable, which lives in your shell, so the code can be shared without it. A key written in the script (a) is published with the code; c and d put the key in the request's content, where it does nothing for authentication.

max_tokens is only a ceiling: a short question gets a short answer that ends on its own with stop_reason "end_turn". Answers a and b treat max_tokens as a target length the model aims for (M8); d treats a generous ceiling as an error.

The API is stateless, so your program writes the model's earlier answer into the list itself, as an "assistant" turn, before appending the next user question. Answer b assumes the API remembers (M1); a files the model's words as the user's, as if only the model could write assistant turns (M9).
In the reply, content is a list of blocks, so a list has no .upper() and Python raises an AttributeError; the text is reply.content[0].text. Answer b treats content as the reply string (M7).

The third call resends the whole history: question 1 + reply 1 + question 2 + reply 2 + question 3 = 10 + 50 + 10 + 50 + 10 = 130. An answer of 10 sends only the new question (M1); 30 sends the questions without the replies (M9).
